$comment: Minimum number of tests each suite must actually run, asserted by
tools/check-test-count.mjs. A green exit code is not evidence that a
suite ran. Measured on Node 24.21: `node --test test/` runs 0 real
tests and exits 1, but `node --test 'test/*.nope.ts'` runs 0 tests and
exits 0. One typo in a glob turns a whole suite into a silent green.
Raise a number here when you add tests. Do not lower one to make CI
green: a drop normally means tests stopped being discovered or stopped
existing, and both are the failure this gate is for.
## The one legitimate decrease: retiring a ledger test
packages/alc/test/known-defects.test.ts pins each open defect from the
adversarial pass (docs/alc-1-attack-report.md) with a test asserting
that the defect STILL REPRODUCES. Those tests are green while the
defect is open and go red when it is fixed, and the failure message is
the instruction: replace the characterisation test with the real
assertion it was standing in for. Defects pinned in the suite that will
own the guarantee behave the same way.
So a fix can legitimately lower this suite's count. One guarantee often
replaces several characterisation tests, and the matching KNOWN_DEFECTS
entry in packages/alc/test/fuzz/invariants.ts goes away with it. That
case was not written down here, which left the only sanctioned
decrease looking exactly like the failure above.
It is still not self-certified. To lower minTests:
1. Follow the protocol in the failing test's message and in the
known-defects.test.ts header in full. Re-measure with the
measurement that found the defect — not with the assertion
flipping. Replace the characterisation test with the guarantee,
under a title that does NOT carry the QA-<n> id. Delete the
KNOWN_DEFECTS entry. Flip the report row to `**fixed** in <sha>`
and fix the counts sentence under the table. Skip a step and the
suite goes red naming the step you skipped.
2. Re-measure the whole suite and set minTests to the count actually
observed on the committed tree. Never to a round number, never to
an estimate, and never below what ran.
3. Add a `retirements` entry below: the defect id, the commit that
fixed it, and the count before and after. An undocumented drop in
this file's history reads exactly like the bug this gate catches;
the entry is what makes the drop reviewable instead.
Any decrease that is not a ledger retirement under that protocol: find
the tests.

suites.note: ALC-1 conformance, admissibility and comparison suites plus the DOG-9 frame fixes (conformance 22, admissibility 12, surface 10, compare 10 = 54), the DOG-5 library suites: coverings, prefix range scans, name resolution, the translator and the browser build (covering 14, resolve 14, query 13, translate 9, bundle 7 = 57), and the DOG-7 adversarial suites: parser fuzz, the address-equality guard, the template acceptance gate, precision honesty, the known-defect reproductions and the status-table consistency checks DOG-10 added (precision-honesty 16, template-acceptance 17, equality-guard 10, fuzz 10, known-defects 3 = 56). template-acceptance went 14 -> 17 on DOG-18: retiring QA-13 replaced one characterisation test with four guarantees — the displacement half is declared, no folding fixture answers wrong unflagged, no preset is falsely flagged, and every `lost` fold site is visible at runtime. compare went 9 -> 10 on DOG-11: QA-12's zero-tolerance invariant cannot see the geometry it was fixed with, because the structural short-circuit answers that case on its own, so `samePlace: the separation it compares against the tolerance is the true one` pins the separation itself against a re-derivation from the cell boxes. precision-honesty went 14 -> 16 and known-defects 4 -> 3 on DOG-16: retiring QA-3, QA-4, QA-8 and QA-11 replaced four characterisation tests with five guarantees, and known-defects.test.ts now holds no characterisation test at all — only the three status-table consistency checks. Every one of those three retirements RAISED this count, so none of them is a ledger-retirement decrease. conformance went 21 -> 22, fuzz 9 -> 10 and known-defects 6 -> 4 on DOG-17: retiring QA-5 and QA-7 moved two characterisation tests out of known-defects and replaced each with the guarantee it stood in for, in the suite that owns it -- the check symbol in conformance, the ASCII trust boundary in fuzz. Net zero across the three files, which is why the floor did not move for that change. Per-file counts are stated so that a drop can be localised without bisecting, and the three group sums are stated so they can be checked against the floor: 54 + 57 + 56 = 167, measured file by file on the committed tree.

DOG-36 stage-A viewer core, DOG-49 stage B, DOG-68's corpus declaration, DOG-71 label state, DOG-78 the curated corpus resolved at load. honesty 32, journey 26, address-equality 6, real-assets 41, research 29, curated-corpus 22, shim-surface 10 = 166, measured file by file on the committed tree. A NEW suite rather than a change to the alc floor: these test packages/atlas-web/src/viewer, which is viewer behaviour, not library behaviour. honesty.test.js pins the five locate() findings to five distinct messages and includes the negative controls -- the three folded cells are asserted CLEAN on anat-adult-p50, so a viewer that flagged everything would fail rather than pass. journey.test.js runs the DOG-1 7 journey as one ordered test, because what it asserts is that camera and layer state survive the brain-atlas round trip, which a per-step test cannot see. address-equality.test.js reuses packages/alc/test/guards/addressEquality.ts against this package's .js sources and keeps an EMPTY reviewed-exception list, plus a planted-violation test so the scanner is never silently inert. QA's independent oracle on DOG-38 lives in packages/atlas-qa and is deliberately NOT merged with this: the value is in the two disagreeing. Raised 51 -> 58 when DOG-35's licence verdict made BV unnamed: a frame with no name index is a different answer from a frame with no matches, and seven tests pin that -- covered:false, no borrowed index version, a distinct info notice, unclaimedFraction 0 rather than resolve()'s 1, exact millimetres still returned, BD still covered, and coverage read off the index rather than declared. Raised 58 -> 121 by DOG-49 stage B: real-assets.test.js runs the same viewer against the templates and name index the asset pipeline emits, read off disk as data and passed through the real validators. A separate file rather than more honesty.test.js cases because the subject differs -- honesty.test.js asserts what the viewer does given a template, real-assets.test.js asserts that the one template v1 ships satisfies the interface that behaviour was written against. Its precision cases state no digit count anywhere: the real body template declares maxUsefulDigits 2 where the default fixture declares 5, so every limit is read off the bound template, and one case re-runs the same address against a doctored cap of 1 to prove a literal would have failed. The 41 are binding 6, naming contract 4, the two-document join 5, precision 7, true extent 4, BV-unnamed 6, deep links 4, notice surface 5 = 41. research.test.js is the other half of stage B: the 7 journey's middle three steps -- region research, a paper revealing all its regions, comparing papers -- which stage A loaded data for and did not implement. Its subject is the rule those steps exist to protect: an anatomical filter narrows the paper LIST and never a selected paper's own mappings. Encoded structurally, so revealPaper() has no filter parameter that can remove a row, and asserted both ways round -- a paper mapped more coarsely than the selection is still found, and a cross-atlas paper's brain mapping survives a thoracic filter. The equality guard caught two real identity comparisons on addresses in the first draft of comparePapers(); onlyA/onlyB are now derived with the same overlaps() predicate `shared` is built from. Raised 121 -> 128 by DOG-68: research.test.js 22 -> 29 for the corpus declaration. This repo holds two research datasets -- the 5-paper fixture this page serves and DOG-37's curated 30-paper seed set the QA oracle reads -- and nothing in the artefact distinguished them, so a section 7 row could drive the page, find FXP-1 and report pass against invented papers. researchModel() now requires `role` to be fixture or curated and requires a fixture to carry its caveat; both fallbacks are refused rather than defaulted, because `fixture` would label the curated corpus invented and `curated` would present invented papers as literature. Two of the seven are must-pass cases in the sense seed.test.js uses: `refuses a role it does not recognise` and `refuses a fixture corpus that gives no caveat` are what stop the validator being satisfied by any string at all, and `keeps the version string and the role saying the same thing` pins the pair build.mjs refuses to emit. Raised 128 -> 134 by DOG-71, which moved label visibility out of app.js's `ui` object and into the viewer state, per atlas and in the deep link. Six tests in journey.test.js, and three of them exist because the default makes this facet easy to fake: labels default ON, so a restore that simply returned the default would pass a one-sided check. `restores labels that were ON when the view was left` is the other side of the journey's own OFF case; `carries label visibility, and only when it is not the default` pins that an unstated `labels` encodes as the default rather than as off, so a view object built before the facet existed does not read as a request to hide them; and `says what it rejected in labels=` pins the allow-list decode, because "0" is a truthy string and a truthiness decoder reads labels=0 as ON -- the one spelling a hand-written link will use. The other three are the per-atlas round trip through encodeView/decodeView, the assertion that toggling labels moves no other facet, and the unknown-atlas refusal. Raised 134 -> 155 by DOG-78: curated-corpus.test.js is a new file, 21 tests, measuring what the curated 30-paper dataset yields when it meets the real name index in the browser. A new file rather than more research.test.js cases because the subject differs in the same way real-assets.test.js differs from honesty.test.js: research.test.js asserts the viewer's corpus-independent BEHAVIOUR against the fixture, this file asserts a MEASUREMENT -- 31 of 170 mappings, 10 of 30 papers, 24 of 120 findings, 139 unplaced, 1741 cells painted. Those are asserted as literals because the failure they guard is silent: a join bug takes every count to zero and renders a paper list with nothing painted, which is exactly what the CORRECT page looks like for the 139 mappings that genuinely cannot be placed. There is no visual difference between 'twenty papers legitimately have no geometry' and 'the join broke', so a number is the only thing that tells them apart. Two of the 21 are must-pass cases in the sense seed.test.ts uses. `would say "unknown structure" for an id declared against this very index` re-partitions the brain ids as `real` and asserts all 135 then DO report unknown-structure -- without it, the neighbouring `never tells a reader the structure is unknown` would be satisfied by a module that had simply deleted the words, and the genuine mistyped-accession case DOG-46 reserved them for would be reported as a licence problem. `paints no cell outside the coverings the index supplied` checks all 25 region-level resolutions by SET MEMBERSHIP on the cell key rather than by overlaps(), because the question is provenance and not geometry: an overlap test would accept a fabricated cell that merely fell inside a real structure, which is the fallback the issue forbids. `matches the resolution the catalogue declares and the index publishes` is what keeps CURATED_CORPUS_RESOLUTION from rotting -- the build cannot measure it, since rule 6 keeps the name index out of dist/data/, so it is declared in the catalogue and re-measured here. Raised 155 -> 156 when R2 wired the curated corpus into the page: `no module the browser loads names a paper from the invented corpus` scans all of src/ for `FXP-` and `example.invalid`, because build.mjs mirrors src/ into dist/app/ and the acceptance criterion is that neither marker appears anywhere in dist/. The build already refuses to EMIT a research document carrying either, which covers dist/data/; this covers the half a doc comment can reintroduce, and two of them had. It carries its own anti-vacuity check: it asserts the markers are still present in fixtures/fixtures.mjs, so deleting the fixture cannot make the scan pass by leaving nothing to find. Raised 156 -> 166 by DOG-84, which made the browser's research bundle a SUBSET of the package: dist/app/atlas-research.js is built from packages/atlas-research/src/index.viewer.ts and exports the three names corpus.js imports, where src/atlas-research.js still re-exports all 24 for Node and this suite. That recovers 8,702 B of gzip on a bundleGzipBytes line reading 98% of 150 KiB, and the price is a failure mode no test in this package could previously have: an import of a name only Node has typechecks, passes every suite here, and throws SyntaxError on the real page. shim-surface.test.js is 10 tests on the scanner that catches it. A new file rather than more address-equality.test.js cases because the subject differs, but it is the same shape of thing and shares that file's discipline: the scanner is imported from ../shim-surface.mjs rather than restated, so the suite's copy cannot drift into leniency, and FOUR of the ten plant a violation, because a scanner over a tree that happens to be clean is indistinguishable from a scanner whose regex matches nothing. The planted name is `browseByAnatomy` -- a real export of @gstack/atlas-research, genuinely absent from the viewer entry -- so the case is the exact mistake the gate exists for and not a synthetic stand-in. Two more are the non-vacuity half rather than assertions about the scanner: `still has a site for the scan to find` fails on zero sites, which is the state the whole arrangement is inert in and is reachable by renaming the shim, and it pins the site list to src/viewer/corpus.js:93 so a second module naming the research layer is a decision rather than a diff nobody reads. `keeps the Node-side shim exporting the WHOLE package` is clause 3 of the restated invariant: narrowing that file to match the browser would take browse, the colour layers and the validator surface away from the 156 tests above, and turn a bundling decision into an API change. The build makes the same check over the EMITTED dist/app/ tree against the emitted bundle's own Object.keys(); this one runs in test:counted, which npm run ci runs before build, so the cheap failure comes first and names a file in src/.

The DOG-1 section 7 journey and the deep-link matrix (DOG-38), authored before the viewer exists. Four files: matrix integrity 14, the oracle cross-check 15, the negative control 9, the UNVERIFIED rule 11, the UI-level address-equality guard 7 = 56, measured file by file on the committed tree.

This floor is doing something slightly different from the alc one. Most of these tests do not drive a build at all -- they ask whether the matrix is still an ENUMERATION and whether the rules the harness is built on still hold. The matrix-integrity file spells out all eighteen cases DOG-38 names as literal row ids, so reorganising the case classes cannot quietly drop one; the oracle file re-derives every pinned address and flag from the library, so a template or library change reports the matrix as stale rather than letting it assert history; the negative-control file runs thirteen deliberately broken builds and requires each to be caught by the case that declares it owns it.

The suite that EXECUTES the matrix against a build is `npm run qa:journey`, and it is deliberately not in the blocking chain: with no product build to point at it would be permanently exit 2 (UNVERIFIED), and a job that is always the same colour stops being read. Task 7 (DOG-39) turns it on with --strict. Until then, the floor here is what stops the authored half silently ceasing to run -- which is the exact failure the issue was created by.

The DOG-37 research layer: the schema validator, both browse modes, the solid-colour layer computation, the trust boundary, the curated seed set, and the browser build. Per-file counts on the committed tree, so a drop can be localised without bisecting: schema 33, browse 20, layers 28, trust 16, seed 18, citations 9, bundle 12 = 136. Raised 124 -> 133 on DOG-76, which added bundle.test.ts: the browser build for this package, in the same position packages/alc/test/bundle.test.ts holds for alc. dist/ is generated and not committed, so the file RUNS scripts/build.mjs and then exercises the output, which is also how the build reaches `npm run ci` -- test:counted runs before build, so no stale artifact can ship, and nothing else in the chain would notice if the build broke. Its subject is the one decision in that build: @gstack/alc is external, imported from './alc.js', not inlined, because two copies of alc in one page are two identity WeakMaps and buildResearchIndex() then rejects a NameIndex the page built with the other copy. That is a fourth must-pass case in this suite, and an unusually direct one -- `an index built by a second copy of alc is rejected` builds an index with alc's own browser bundle, a genuinely separate module, and requires the refusal, so the accepting case above it cannot be vacuously green. Two more of the nine are non-vacuity checks rather than assertions about the build: the resolution comparison is repeated against a name index with one mapped structure removed, and the test asserts that removal really did move a mapping from `resolved` to `unknown-structure`, because mapping-by-mapping equality over a dataset that resolves everywhere says nothing about `unresolvedReason`. Raised 113 -> 124 on DOG-46, which is a correction as much as an addition: DOG-50 added citations.test.ts without moving the floor, so nine tests were running unprotected and deleting that whole file would have left this gate green. Two of the eleven are DOG-46's own, both in schema.test.ts: a partitioned dataset must say per structure which index should name it, and structureIdSources must describe the namespaces the mappings actually use. Three of those files carry a must-pass case, and the floor is only meaningful while they do. browse.test.ts has `the leak detector would catch a leak`, which builds a selection deliberately intersected with the anatomical filter and asserts the comparison used by the filter-leak test can see the difference — without it, that test would pass against an implementation that leaked. seed.test.ts has `the resolution check can fail`, which points a mapping at a structure id the index does not have and asserts it surfaces as `unknown-structure` painting nothing. layers.test.ts pins the palette's exact hexes and slot order, because the order is the colour-vision safety mechanism and re-ordering it is a measurement rather than a preference. Deleting any of those three lowers the count and removes the evidence that the gate above it can go red. Raised 133 -> 136 on DOG-84, which added a third output: dist/atlas-research.viewer.js, built from src/index.viewer.ts, exporting the three names packages/atlas-web/src/viewer/corpus.js imports. 8,702 B of gzip off a bundleGzipBytes line reading 98% of 150 KiB. It is not three extra cases -- it is a restatement, and the three replace the one test that said `both outputs export exactly what the source does`. That sentence was right while every output had the same extent and is wrong now that one deliberately does not, so each output is paired with the ENTRY it was built from and checked for exact equality against that. The other two are what stop the restatement being a weakening. `the viewer entry is a proper subset of the package, binding for binding` compares by IDENTITY, because a name check is satisfied by a reimplementation and the whole argument for serving a subset is that it is the same code reached through a shorter path; its properness assertion is the one that catches the trim being quietly undone, since an index.viewer.ts grown back to all 24 names would pass every other check in the file while re-spending the headroom. `the viewer bundle stopped containing the modules it stopped reaching` reads the emitted `__m_*` module scopes off the output and asserts browse.ts and layers.ts are absent from it and present in the full bundle, so the claim the change rests on is measured rather than inferred from a byte count. The behavioural comparisons deliberately do NOT skip the viewer bundle: its three names are compared against the source like everything else, and only the cases that name a browse.ts or layers.ts export are restricted to the full-surface outputs -- a bundle that is merely smaller and also wrong passes a size check and fails these. `the three exports the viewer gets behave identically in every output` exists because formatCitation would otherwise be the one name the page actually uses that nothing in this file compares. Re-measured on the DOG-111 merge of DOG-84 (a83d527) with DOG-76's final tip (525b51a): 136, not 133 + 3 added up. 525b51a rewrote the body of an existing case (`alc is external`) and added none, so the union is DOG-84's 136; the merged `alc is external` now runs DOG-76's every-alc-export declaration scan over BOTH single-file bundles.
